# Tool reference: SimCity 4 server (simcity4)

<!-- generated by scripts/gen_tool_docs.py from the server's tools/list; do not edit by hand -->

47 tools. Every tool takes JSON arguments as described and returns compact JSON text, except `guide` (markdown). Failures are MCP tool errors (`isError: true`) whose text is JSON `{"error": ..., "hint": ...}`.

Kinds map to the MCP tool annotations each tool carries:

| kind | readOnlyHint | destructiveHint | idempotentHint | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| read | True | False | True | reads the game, changes nothing |
| observe | True | False | False | reads; has a 'since last call' cursor |
| set | False | False | True | sets a value (idempotent) |
| act | False | False | False | acts in the game |
| destructive | False | True | False | can discard or destroy something (unsaved city, a file, the game process) |

All tools have openWorldHint false (they act on the local game only).

## Server instructions

Sent to the client at initialization:

> Tools for playing SimCity 4 Deluxe (1.1.641) through the game's own code. Start with guide(), then game_launch(). Coordinates are city cells; regions are grids of city tiles. Every result is JSON; failures are tool errors with {error, hint}.

## guide

*read*

How to use this server: the guide for agents, by topic.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `topic` | string | `'start'` | "start" (overview and first steps), "all" (the whole guide) or a section name such as "regions". |

## game_launch

*act*

Start SimCity 4 (or attach to the instance SiMCP started earlier) and connect to it. The game runs without administrator rights and with SiMCP's own user folder (its own Regions and settings; the player's plugins are mirrored, so the simulation is the same), and opens on the region view. Returns the game status.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `windowed` | boolean | `true` | run in a window (true) or full screen. |
| `width` | integer | `1024` | window / screen width in pixels (screen recipes are measured at 1024x768). |
| `height` | integer | `768` | window / screen height in pixels. |
| `intro` | boolean | `false` | play the intro movie. |
| `timeout_s` | integer | `120` | seconds to wait for the game to finish starting. |

## game_status

*read*

Whether SimCity 4 is running and controllable, and what it shows (region view or a city).

No parameters.

## list_regions

*read*

The regions in SiMCP's user folder with their city tiles (grid position, size small / medium / large) and each tile's saved city (name, mayor, established or not, populations). Reads files: works without the game.

No parameters.

## load_region

*act*

Open a region in the region view (the game's own LoadRegion). Works from the region view; leave a city first.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the region's folder name as list_regions shows it (e.g. "MCP Test", "Timbuktu"). |

## load_city

*act*

Open a city of the loaded region with the region view's own LoadCity: with a name, the founded city of that name; without one, the first unfounded tile of the given size (it opens in god mode: terrain only). Returns the city's status.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | `''` | a founded city's name as list_regions shows it, or "" for an unfounded tile. |
| `size` | string | `'any'` | for an unfounded tile: "small" (64x64 cells), "medium" (128x128), "large" (256x256) or "any". |

## found_city

*act*

Found (establish) the unfounded tile that is open, as the player does: the Mayor Mode button, then the Establish City dialog with the city's and the mayor's names and the difficulty. After this the god-mode terrain tools are no longer available and the difficulty cannot change (the game's own rule).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the city's name (1-31 characters). |
| `mayor` | string | required | the mayor's name (1-31 characters). |
| `difficulty` | string | `'easy'` | "easy", "medium" or "hard" (sets the starting funds and the economy's difficulty). |

*set*

The game's speed buttons: "slow", "medium" or "fast" (like the buttons, this also un-pauses).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `speed` | string | required | "slow", "medium" or "fast". |

## set_paused

*set*

Pause or resume the simulation with the game's pause button.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `paused` | boolean | required | true to pause, false to run. |

## save_city

*destructive*

Save the open city with the game's own save, into its file in SiMCP's user folder (replacing the previous save). SiMCP's copies of the cities shipped with the game are kept as shipped unless allow_shipped.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow_shipped` | boolean | `false` | also save over SiMCP's copy of a city that came with the game. |

## dialog_status

*read*

The game's open dialog windows, topmost first: title, texts and buttons (labels and ids). When a dialog is open the game waits for an answer; close_dialog answers it.

No parameters.

## close_dialog

*act*

Answer the topmost dialog by pressing one of its buttons, as the player clicks it.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `button` | string | required | the button's label as dialog_status shows it (case-insensitive; a unique part is enough) or its id. |

## set_popups

*set*

Whether the game opens popup windows (advisor messages, message boxes) during play. With popups off the game keeps running unattended; advice still reaches the advisors panel and news (read them with advisors()).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | required | true = the game's normal popups, false = none. |

## leave_city

*destructive*

Go back to the region view without saving (unsaved changes to the city are lost).

No parameters.

## advance_time

*act*

Advance the open city by this many game days and pause exactly on the target day.

mode "natural" (default) lets the game play at its fast speed - everything happens as for a player who presses fast and waits (buildings finish construction, cars drive, idle work runs), about 10-20 days per second. "unthrottled" removes the game's spacing between days (much faster, but buildings finish on wall-clock time in this game, so fewer complete per day). "exact" steps days with the game's day code under a hidden pause (fastest and fully deterministic per day; construction barely progresses - use it for budget / time checks). The player's speed and pause state are restored. If max_seconds runs out first, remaining_days says how many days are left.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `days` | integer | `1` | game days to advance (1 or more). |
| `mode` | string | `'natural'` | natural, unthrottled or exact. |
| `max_seconds` | number | `90.0` | wall-clock limit for this call (keep it under your client's tool timeout). |

## city_status

*read*

The open city: name, mayor, founded or not, difficulty, size in cells, the game date, speed and pause state, read from the game's memory; and how many cheats SiMCP has used in it (cheat log).

No parameters.

## map_data

*read*

One data layer of the open city as a grid, read from the game's memory: the values the game's data views and simulation use. Call with no layer to list the layers. Values are per tract (tract_size cells square; rows[z][x] in tract units); a cell (x, z) is in tract (x // tract_size, z // tract_size).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `layer` | string | `''` | a layer name ("zones", "land_value", "crime", "police_coverage", "fire_coverage", "air_pollution", "water_pollution", "garbage", "power", "water", "traffic_congestion", "mayor_rating", ...); "" lists them. |
| `x0` | integer | `0` | first cell column of the area to return (0 = west edge). |
| `z0` | integer | `0` | first cell row of the area to return. |
| `x1` | integer | `-1` | last cell column (inclusive; -1 = the city's edge). |
| `z1` | integer | `-1` | last cell row (inclusive; -1 = the city's edge). |

## tile_info

*read*

Everything about one cell of the open city: the value of every data layer there, the terrain altitude at its corners, water depth and sea level, and the lot / building standing on it. Read from memory.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | required | cell column (0 = west edge). |
| `z` | integer | required | cell row (0 = north edge). |

## get_budget

*read*

The city's money: funds, the tax rate of every zone and wealth group, this month's income and expenses, last month's, year to date, the game's end-of-year estimate, and loans. Read from the game.

No parameters.

## set_tax

*set*

Set the tax rate of one zone and wealth group, as the Budget window's spinners do (0.0 to 20.0 percent in steps of 0.1; outside values are clamped). Returns the rate the game now uses.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | string | required | one of residential_low, residential_medium, residential_high, commercial_services_low, commercial_services_medium, commercial_services_high, commercial_office_medium, commercial_office_high, industrial_agriculture, industrial_dirty, industrial_manufacturing, industrial_high_tech. |
| `rate` | number | required | the tax rate in percent. |

## departments

*read*

The city's budget departments (police, fire, health, education, transit, utilities...): funding percentage, the most the player may set, and this month's expense and income for each.

No parameters.

## set_department_funding

*set*

Set a department's funding, as the Budget window's slider does (0 up to the department's maximum, usually 120 percent; clamped). Lower funding saves money but weakens the service. Returns the new monthly expense.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `department` | string | required | the department's name as departments() lists it (e.g. "Police Dept.", "Education"; a unique part of the name is enough) or its id. |
| `percent` | number | required | the funding in percent of the full cost. |

## ordinances

*read*

Every ordinance the game knows (including those added by plugins): whether it is available to this city, enacted, its enactment and repeal fees, its current monthly income or cost, and its description.

No parameters.

## set_ordinance

*set*

Enact or repeal an ordinance, as the Ordinances panel does (only ordinances available to the city). Fees and monthly effects are settled with the month's budget.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the ordinance's name as ordinances() lists it (a unique part of the name is enough) or its id. |
| `enacted` | boolean | required | true to enact, false to repeal. |

## loans

*read*

The city's loans (principal, monthly payment, what is left to pay, when they end) and the bank's limits.

No parameters.

## take_loan

*act*

Take a loan from the bank, as the Loans window does: 5,000 to 100,000 in steps of 5,000, within the game's limits (number of loans and total borrowing). The money is added to the funds at once; it is repaid monthly with interest (SimCity 4 has no early repayment).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | integer | required | the loan amount. |

## demand

*read*

Residential, commercial and industrial demand per wealth group, as the game's demand graph shows it, with the share blocked by caps, plus the number of residents.

No parameters.

## lots

*read*

The lots of the open city with their building: position, size, facing, zone, wealth, state (occupied, abandoned, under construction...), historical, power, and the building's name and exemplar id.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zone` | string | `''` | only lots of this zone (e.g. "residential_low", "industrial_high", "plopped"); "" = all. |
| `x0` | integer | `0` | west edge of the area (cells). |
| `z0` | integer | `0` | north edge of the area (cells). |
| `x1` | integer | `-1` | east edge (inclusive; -1 = the city's edge). |
| `z1` | integer | `-1` | south edge (inclusive; -1 = the city's edge). |
| `limit` | integer | `500` | at most this many lots in the answer (count always gives the total). |

## advisors

*read*

What the city's advisors say now: each advisor's mood and current messages (title, mood, priority, text) - the same advice the game shows in its advisor panel, popups and news ticker.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `include_fluff` | boolean | `false` | also list the fluffy news (jokes without game meaning). |

## build_menu

*read*

What the player can plop now, from the game's build menus (with plugins): each item's name, lot and building ids, menus, size in cells, plop cost, monthly cost, and whether the menu offers it (available=false: greyed - a locked reward, a population or era requirement, an exclusion). menu="trees" lists the trees.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `menu` | string | `''` | one menu only: parks, transport, ferry, power, water, garbage, police, jail, fire, education, health, airports, landmarks, rewards, other, or trees. "" = all. |

## plop

*act*

Plop a building from the build menus, as the player's plop tool does: the game's placement rules apply and its plop cost is charged. Refused when the menu greys it out (locked reward, requirement not met) or the spot is taken, too steep or under water (nothing is charged then).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `building` | string | required | a name from build_menu ("Coal Power Plant") or its lot or building id ("0x02000002"). |
| `x` | integer | required | west edge of the lot (cell). |
| `z` | integer | required | north edge of the lot (cell). |
| `facing` | string | `'north'` | the side the lot's front faces: north (toward smaller z), east, south or west. |

## build_network

*act*

Build a road, rail, pipe, power line or other network through cells, as the player drags it: one drag per leg between consecutive points, laid by the game's own path solver (diagonals and curves as the game makes them), each leg's cost charged to the funds (a leg the city cannot pay is not built).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `network` | string | required | road, street, avenue, one_way_road, rail, light_rail, monorail, subway, elevated_highway, ground_highway, dirt_road, pipe or power_line. |
| `points` | array of array of integer | required | cells [[x, z], ...]: where the drag starts and each point where it bends or ends (2 to 64). |
| `build_it` | boolean | `true` | false = only report each leg's cost and whether the game allows it. |
| `connect_neighbor` | boolean | `false` | at the city edge, accept the game's offer to connect to the neighbour city. |
| `bridge` | integer | `-1` | over water, which of the game's bridge choices to build (index; -1 = the game's default). |

## zone

*act*

Zone (or de-zone) a rectangle of cells, as the player's zone tool does: the game's zoning rules (slope, size) and its cost per cell, charged to the funds. Areas larger than one drag (32 x 32, 48 x 48 for agriculture) are zoned in several drags.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zone_type` | string | required | residential_low, residential_medium, residential_high, commercial_low, commercial_medium, commercial_high, agriculture, industrial_medium, industrial_high, military, airport, seaport, spaceport, landfill, or dezone. |
| `x0` | integer | required | west edge (cell). |
| `z0` | integer | required | north edge (cell). |
| `x1` | integer | required | east edge (cell, inclusive). |
| `z1` | integer | required | south edge (cell, inclusive). |
| `build_it` | boolean | `true` | false = only report the cost. |
| `streets` | boolean | `true` | lay the automatic streets inside large zones (false = the Ctrl-drag). |
| `alternate` | boolean | `false` | the Alt-drag variant of the zone tool. |

## bulldoze

*destructive*

Bulldoze everything on a rectangle of cells (buildings, lots, networks, trees), as the player's bulldozer does: the game's demolition cost is taken from the funds (as in the game, this can go below zero).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x0` | integer | required | west edge (cell). |
| `z0` | integer | required | north edge (cell). |
| `x1` | integer | required | east edge (cell, inclusive). |
| `z1` | integer | required | south edge (cell, inclusive). |
| `build_it` | boolean | `true` | false = only report the cost. |

## plant_trees

*act*

Plant one tree in each cell of a rectangle, as the player's flora tool does: each tree's price is charged, and planting stops when the city cannot pay.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree` | string | required | a tree from build_menu(menu="trees"): its name ("Oak Tree") or id. |
| `x0` | integer | required | west edge (cell). |
| `z0` | integer | required | north edge (cell). |
| `x1` | integer | required | east edge (cell, inclusive). |
| `z1` | integer | required | south edge (cell, inclusive). |
| `build_it` | boolean | `true` | false = only report the cost. |

## graphs

*read*

The game's Graphs window: every graph (mayor rating, funds, income and expenses, population by type and age, demand, power, water, pollution, garbage, commute time, traffic volume, crime, education, life expectancy...) with each line's latest value in the units the window shows. graph_data gives the history of a line.

No parameters.

## graph_data

*read*

The history of one or more series the city keeps (the data behind the Graphs window and the advisors' trends): dated samples, oldest first. Most series get one sample a month; tax rates one a day.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `series` | string | `''` | a graph title ("Funds (000s)", "Crime"), a line ("Power: Capacity"), a series name ("funds", "air_pollution", "tax_rate_residential_low") or an id ("0x4A5BA3D0"). "" lists every series kept. |
| `last` | integer | `24` | the newest this many samples per series (0 = all kept). |

## camera

*read*

Where the city view looks: the centre cell (x, z), the ground altitude there, zoom (1 far .. 6 close), rotation (0..3) and the viewport size in pixels.

No parameters.

## set_camera

*set*

Move the city view as the player does (the game's own view commands); omitted values stay as they are.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | `-1` | centre cell, west-east (-1 = keep). |
| `z` | integer | `-1` | centre cell, north-south (-1 = keep). |
| `zoom` | integer | `0` | 1 (far) to 6 (close); 0 = keep. |
| `rotation` | integer | `-1` | 0..3 (each step is a quarter turn clockwise); -1 = keep. |

## day_night

*set*

The day/night cycle, as god mode's button sets it: day_and_night (the clock runs), day (always day) or night (always night). With no mode it reads the setting.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `''` | day_and_night, day, night, or "" to read. |

## snapshot

*observe*

A picture of the city as the game draws it (the game's own snapshot of its view, with its UI), after moving the view if asked. Returns the camera and the image; the full-size PNG is kept in SiMCP's snapshots folder.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | `-1` | centre cell, west-east (-1 = keep). |
| `z` | integer | `-1` | centre cell, north-south (-1 = keep). |
| `zoom` | integer | `0` | 1 (far) to 6 (close); 0 = keep. |
| `rotation` | integer | `-1` | 0..3; -1 = keep. |
| `width` | integer | `1024` | scale the image to this many pixels wide (the PNG keeps the full size). |

## disaster_status

*read*

Disasters going on in the open city (fires, volcanoes, earthquakes, riots, toxic spills...) with their locations, and the god-mode Disasters menu.

No parameters.

## start_disaster

*act*

Start a disaster from the god-mode Disasters menu at a cell, with the game's own disaster tool (as the player's click). Disasters unfold while the game runs: set_paused(false) or advance_time afterwards.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `disaster` | string | required | volcano, earthquake, fire, meteor, tornado, lightning, robot_attack, autosaurus_wrecks or ufo. |
| `x` | integer | required | cell, west-east. |
| `z` | integer | required | cell, north-south. |

## dispatch

*act*

Send emergency units to a cell with the game's dispatch tools (as the player's dispatch buttons): the city needs a station of that kind with a free unit and a road route to the cell.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unit` | string | required | fire, police, fire_plane or police_helicopter. |
| `x` | integer | required | cell, west-east. |
| `z` | integer | required | cell, north-south. |

## cheat

*act*

Run one of the game's player cheats - outside honest play, so every use is logged (SiMCP's cheats.jsonl) and counted in city_status. Only vetted cheats run, with checked arguments: weaknesspays (+1,000), riskymoney (+10,000, may start a riot), howdryiam (all watered), fightthepower (all powered), barstuck, whattimeizit <hour>, stopwatch pause|resume|magnify <n>, showtime, whererufrom <city name>, hellomynameis <mayor name>, dollyllama, casper [off], gp on|off. Developer and crashing cheats are refused.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the cheat (case-insensitive). |
| `argument` | string | `''` | its argument, if it takes one (a single word for names). |

## city_figures

*read*

The city figures the game computes for its advisors (about 190 game.g_* values: population per zone and wealth, tile and building counts, coverage, congestion, funds, borrowing...), read from the game's own Lua state. With no expression it lists the names; with one it evaluates it, read-only.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `expression` | string | `''` | e.g. "game.g_population", "game.g_road_tile_count + game.g_street_tile_count", "game.trend_value(game_trends.G_FUNDS, 12)". Allowed: game.g_* values, read-only game functions (trend_value, trend_slope, trend_count, ordinance_is_on, difficulty_level...), the constant tables (game_trends, tuning_constants...), numbers, strings, arithmetic, comparisons, and/or/not, tostring, tonumber, math.*. |

## quit_game

*destructive*

Quit SimCity 4 without saving (an open city's unsaved changes are lost; save first if needed).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `force` | boolean | `false` | end the process instead of asking the game to quit (use only if the game no longer responds). |
